newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks rise to firm close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks rise to firm close.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks reversed their earlier downward course to close Wednesday afternoon firmly up due to a return of good buying momentum on rising turnover, brokers said.
"The sell-off this morning was very unconvincing," said Glenn Lesko, head of equities trading at HG Asia."Nobody wants to sell this market."
The Hang Seng Index put on 47.71 points to close at 12,492.37, its high for the day. In the morning session, the index trended as much as 76 points off before reversing course.
Turnover remained comparatively high at HK$6.30 billion, although down from Tuesday's HK$6.67 billion.
"HSBC is responsible for a good part of today's gains," said Lesko.

HSBC, which accounts for about 18 percent of the capitalisation of the index, added another HK$1.50 to close at HK$157.00 after touching a new high of HK$157.50. The share was the most actively traded with relatively heavy turnover of HK$487.50 million.
Despite the market's strong recent gains and the lack of a basebuilding period at higher levels, brokers remain upbeat.
"The market has a chance to test the 12,600 level this week. It's still in a healthy mode," said P.C. Wong, director of Hing Feng Futures.
Wong said the Hang Seng Index could advance to 12,850, its major resistance level, before the U.S. presidential election in early November.

The finance sector led the market, followed by utilities, while the property sector was little changed. The commercial and industrial sector managed only a slight gain, recovering from Tuesday's sell off.
Three large market cap stocks, Hang Seng Bank, Swire Pacific and Citic Pacific which were sold off on Tuesday and rebound in late trading on Wednesday also helped boost the index, brokers said.
Hang Seng Bank rose HK$1.00 to HK$92.00.

Swire Pacific gained HK$1.00 to HK$71.25 and CITIC Pacific added HK$0.30 to HK$37.30. The shares were sold off on Tuesday due to their exposure to Cathay Pacific and fears of higher fuel prices for that airline. Cathay put on HK$0.15 to HK$12.35.
